body.statement: For \(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\), the exact robust deterministic linear-band frontier and the SOCP value satisfy \[W_s\le\Gamma_s\le\left(1+c_\alpha\sqrt{2\sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min}}\right)W_s.\] The factor is independent of \(N\), \(T\), \(K\), \(M\), the adoption pattern, the predictors, and the donor-overlap geometry.
body.justification: A matching upper and lower width comparison turns the conic rule from a convenient band into a decision-theoretic frontier result.
body.gap: ArmstrongKolesar2018 treats scalar linear functionals, and CattaneoFengPalombaTitiunik2025 treats simultaneous staggered prediction without a minimax width comparison across nested simplex faces.
body.consumer: Practitioners can use the tractable SOCP knowing that no deterministic linear synthetic-control rectangle can improve worst-coordinate width beyond the displayed fixed factor.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\).  By
\texttt{thm:socp-coverage}, an optimizing SOCP weight array together with
the deterministic half-widths
\[
 \ell_e=b_e(w)+z_B\operatorname{sd}_e(w)
 \tag{1}
\]
is feasible for the honest-band problem in
\texttt{def:exact-width-frontier}, and its maximum half-width is
\(\Gamma_s\).  Therefore
\[
 W_s\leq\Gamma_s.
 \tag{2}
\]

For the reverse comparison, take an arbitrary feasible pair \((w,\ell)\)
in \texttt{def:exact-width-frontier} and put
\[
 R=\max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e.
 \tag{3}
\]
The standing condition \(\mathcal J\neq\varnothing\), together with
\(K\geq0\), implies \(M=|\mathcal E|\geq1\), so the maximum in (3) and
\(q_\alpha(M)\) are well defined.

We first prove a deterministic bias lower bound.  Suppose for contradiction
that \(b_e(w)>R\) for some coordinate \(e\).  By
\texttt{lem:bias-radius}, there is a law \(P_e\) in the model class under
which the mean of the coordinate error is \(b_e(w)\).  Its variance is
\(\operatorname{sd}_e(w)^2>0\), by
\texttt{lem:contrast-geometry}.  Writing the coordinate error as
\(b_e(w)+\operatorname{sd}_e(w)G\), where \(G\sim N(0,1)\), and using
\(\ell_e\leq R<b_e(w)\), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_e\{|\widehat\tau_e(w)-\tau_e|\leq\ell_e\}
 &\leq P_e\{\widehat\tau_e(w)-\tau_e\leq\ell_e\}\\
 &=\Phi\!\left(
    \frac{\ell_e-b_e(w)}{\operatorname{sd}_e(w)}\right)
 <\frac12.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
The simultaneous coverage probability is no larger than this marginal
probability.  Equation (4) contradicts uniform coverage at least
\(1-\alpha>1/2\).  Hence
\[
 \max_{e\in\mathcal E}b_e(w)\leq R.
 \tag{5}
\]

We next prove the stochastic lower bound without imposing independence on the
actual contrasts.  Choose any \(e_0\in\mathcal E\).  The endpoint-attainment
part of \texttt{lem:bias-radius} supplies at least one model-class law
\(P_0\).  Under this law, \texttt{lem:prediction-error} represents the full
error vector as
\[
 \widehat\tau(w)-\tau=\mu+Z,
 \qquad
 Z\sim N(0,V),
 \qquad
 V=A(w)\Sigma_QA(w)^{\top}.
 \tag{6}
\]
By \texttt{lem:contrast-geometry},
\[
 V\succeq\sigma_{\min}I_M.
 \tag{7}
\]
Set \(C=V-\sigma_{\min}I_M\succeq0\).  A spectral decomposition of \(C\)
constructs a possibly singular Gaussian vector \(U\sim N(0,C)\).  On a
product probability space, take it independent of
\(X\sim N(0,\sigma_{\min}I_M)\).  Then \(X+U\) has covariance \(V\), so it
has the same centered Gaussian law as \(Z\).

Write \(s_0=\sqrt{\sigma_{\min}}>0\).  For \(R>0\) and \(u\in\mathbb R\),
define
\[
 g_R(u)=P\{|s_0G+u|\leq R\}
 =\Phi\!\left(\frac{R-u}{s_0}\right)
  +\Phi\!\left(\frac{R+u}{s_0}\right)-1.
 \tag{8}
\]
This function is even.  For \(u\geq0\), differentiation gives
\[
 g_R'(u)=\frac1{s_0}\left\{
 \varphi\!\left(\frac{R+u}{s_0}\right)
 -\varphi\!\left(\frac{R-u}{s_0}\right)\right\}\leq0,
 \tag{9}
\]
because \(|R+u|\geq|R-u|\) and the standard normal density is decreasing
as a function of absolute value.  Thus \(g_R(u)\leq g_R(0)\) for every real
\(u\).  Conditional on \(U=u\), the coordinates of \(X\) are independent;
therefore (8)--(9), applied with the deterministic shifts \(u_k+\mu_k\),
give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P\{\mu+X+U\in[-R,R]^M\mid U=u\}
 &=\prod_{k=1}^M g_R(u_k+\mu_k)\\
 &\leq g_R(0)^M
 =P\{X\in[-R,R]^M\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
Integration over the possibly degenerate law of \(U\) proves the same
inequality unconditionally.  For \(R=0\), both cube probabilities involving
the nonsingular vector \(X\) are zero, so the inequality also holds at the
boundary.

The coverage rectangle for \((w,\ell)\) is contained in \([-R,R]^M\).
Applying honesty under the particular law \(P_0\), then (6) and (10), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 1-\alpha
 &\leq P_0\{|\widehat\tau_e(w)-\tau_e|\leq\ell_e
              \text{ for every }e\in\mathcal E\}\\
 &\leq P_0\{\widehat\tau(w)-\tau\in[-R,R]^M\}\\
 &\leq P\{X\in[-R,R]^M\}\\
 &=P\left\{\max_{1\leq k\leq M}|G_k|
       \leq\frac{R}{\sqrt{\sigma_{\min}}}\right\},
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
where the \(G_k\) in the last line are independent standard normals.  The
right side of (11) is zero at \(R=0\) and is strictly increasing in its
nonnegative threshold.  The definition of \(q_\alpha(M)\) therefore yields
\[
 R\geq\sqrt{\sigma_{\min}}\,q_\alpha(M).
 \tag{12}
\]

By the coordinate upper bound in \texttt{lem:contrast-geometry} and by
\texttt{lem:gaussian-quantile-ratio}, respectively,
\[
 \operatorname{sd}_e(w)\leq\sqrt{2\sigma_{\max}}
 \quad(e\in\mathcal E),
 \qquad
 z_B\leq c_\alpha q_\alpha(M).
 \tag{13}
\]
Using (5), (12), and (13) in the variational characterization of
\(\Gamma_s\) proved in \texttt{thm:socp-coverage} gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Gamma_s
 &\leq\max_{e\in\mathcal E}
       \{b_e(w)+z_B\operatorname{sd}_e(w)\}\\
 &\leq R+c_\alpha q_\alpha(M)\sqrt{2\sigma_{\max}}\\
 &\leq\left(1+c_\alpha
       \sqrt{\frac{2\sigma_{\max}}{\sigma_{\min}}}\right)R.
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]
The feasible pair \((w,\ell)\) was arbitrary.  Taking its infimum in (14),
as prescribed by \texttt{def:exact-width-frontier}, and combining with (2)
proves
\[
 W_s\leq\Gamma_s\leq
 \left(1+c_\alpha
 \sqrt{\frac{2\sigma_{\max}}{\sigma_{\min}}}\right)W_s.
\]
The denominator is positive by the declared covariance-band parameter domain.
There is no asymptotic or limit condition.  The multiplier depends only on
the fixed \(\alpha\) and covariance-band ratio, and hence not on any of the
dimensions, adoption pattern, predictors, or donor-overlap geometry listed
in the claim.
